(2) Custom Python blocked Cholesky (batched diag+panel+trailing) is 3x SLOWER (11600us) -- cuSOLVER's single fused persistent kernel beats any multi-launch blocking (same lesson as the recon's cuBLAS-trsm). (3) TF32-trailing Cholesky BREAKS positive-definiteness (cond(G)=3.2e8 needs FP64 Schur). (4) CholeskyQR2 (2x FP32 potrf, passes orth) is WORSE: potrf is panel-bound so 2xFP32potrf(6452) + extra R-solve(2284) >> 1xFP64potrf(3574). cuSOLVER FP64 potrf IS the right tool. ATTACKED THE R-SOLVE (candidate b, 2284us): also at floor. (a) nb sweep: nb=384 is the speed optimum among orth-PASSING values (nb=512 is 68us faster but FAILS orth 115>100; orth is non-monotonic in nb as documented). B200 has no FP32 tensor cores so the diagonal solve is stuck on SIMT. Trailing already 3xTF32 (1xTF32 documented to blow orth ~3.5). ATTACKED HOST ROUND-TRIPS (candidate c): NO headroom -- the path is GPU-bound (stage timings == GPU-busy from nsys, no gap); int_mm loop (14 calls, 798us) is INT8 tensor cores back-to-back; Gram recombine (522us FP64) can't be coalesced cheaper (a P-layout repack costs 668us, MORE than the recombine). KEY HARNESS FINDING: the diff_correctness guard tests shape6 at OFFSET seeds (33421..) NOT the benchmark seed 32412, and the two disagree at the orth margin (3xTF32 passed guard but failed bench-seed; 4xTF32 passed bench-seed but failed guard) -- the binding gate is the benchmark check, so a candidate must pass BOTH; the guard alone under-tests shape6. SUGGESTIONS FOR NEXT BRIEFS: (1) The recon (orhr_col LU, 6585us/47%) is now BY FAR the biggest shape6 piece and the real prize -- my prior brief optimized only its diag_lu (the global-best diag_lu_reg win); the recon's cuBLAS-trsm panels + TF32 Schur deserve a fresh dedicated brief (prior 'at floor' was for the right-looking structure -- a LEFT-looking or 2-level recon, or a fundamentally different reflector-extraction, may help). (2) A TSQR/comm-avoiding Householder QR that emits (H,tau) DIRECTLY would skip BOTH the R-solve AND the entire recon (the 47%+16%=63% of shape6 that exist only to convert explicit-Q to compact form) -- env.md lists CAQR/TSQR as 'dead ends' for B=2 underfill, but those targeted FULL replacement; a hybrid that uses CholeskyQR for R but a cheap direct reflector extraction (avoiding orhr_col's explicit-Q LU) is unexplored. (3) Shape6 is ~14ms but only 1/12 shapes; geomean sensitivity d(geomean)/geomean = (1/12)*d(s6)/s6, so even a 1ms shape6 cut is only ~0.6% geomean -- the leaderboard gap should decide whether shape6 is worth more workers vs the n=512/1024 groups that dominate the geomean.

(A) MATH: a closed-form (H,tau) extraction from (Q,R) that skips the orhr_col LU is IMPOSSIBLE, proven numerically. The compact reflector vectors V are the strict-lower of LU(M), M=Q-diag(D). I verified: (1) the LU's upper factor U is NOT derivable from R -- |U - R*D| is large and U_ii/R_ii is non-constant (0.07..-0.13), so there is no V=f(Q,R) cheaper than the full O(n^3/3) elimination; (2) the sign diagonal D is NOT free either (D != -sign(diag(Q)), diff=2.0) -- it requires the LU's diagonal evolution. There is no third path: you either run geqrf on A directly (the dead underfilled-panel path) or form explicit Q then orhr_col LU (current). The 'WY representation' the brief suggested still needs the O(n^3) elimination. The R-solve produces Q and CANNOT be skipped -- the reflectors must reproduce that explicit Q.

(B) ROOT CAUSE of the recon's 6585us: it is LAUNCH-LATENCY bound at batch=2, NOT flop-bound. Measured: the recon runs at ~7 TFLOP/s on a ~1000+ TFLOP/s B200 (B=2 -> ~2 CTAs, ~146 SMs idle); the Schur GEMM is 95% of flops but only ~2401us of the 6585; the other ~3683us is the 2 cublasStrsm/panel LOOPED per matrix (4 launches/panel x 63 = 252 calls). KEY: each cublasStrsm is ~14.5us CONSTANT from rest=64 to rest=4032 -- pure launch latency, not compute. So the lever is FEWER LAUNCHES, but every alternative adds launches or slows a piece:
 - iter1/2 Custom fused-TRSM kernels (1 launch/panel, both matrices, device-filling): SLOWER -- uncoalesced strided per-thread substitution; FP32 fails the orth margin (seed 39475: 0.0587>0.0488), FP64 accum fixes it but B200 FP64 is 16x slower (shape6 14875), Kahan FP32 also slower (16084).
 - cublasStrsmBatched (4->2 launches): cuBLAS EXECUTION_FAILED (status 13/14) on the in-place strided sub-block pointers; also less accurate (test.5 orth 68.5 vs 60).
 - iter3 Inverse-then-GEMM (invert 64x64 diag block, apply by FP32 batched GEMM): CORRECT and bit-identical-precise (test.5 orth=60 == parent; the 64x64 triangular inverse + FP32 GEMM matches TRSM exactly, verified). GEMM apply MATH is faster (~7.5us vs 14.5us) BUT needs inverse + 2 gather + 2 GEMM = 5 launches/panel vs 4 TRSM -> MORE launches -> slower (15057).
 - iter4 ob=128 wider panel (32 vs 63 panels -> HALF the launches; diag_lu_dyn_kernel, 64KB dynamic smem): validation PASS, orth=44.5 (BETTER than parent -- fewer TF32 Schur steps). But shape6 16322 -- the 128-wide diag_lu uses the SLOW smem path (whole block through smem each column), smem-bandwidth-bound, far slower than 2x the 64-wide REGISTER-blocked diag_lu (the exact lesson from the prior diag_lu_reg win). Launch savings don't recover the diag_lu cost.

Per layout.md, a gap of MULTIPLES means #1 uses a fundamentally different algorithm our current line cannot reach by shaving shape6. Moreover shape6 is only 1/12 shapes: geomean sensitivity d(geomean)/geomean = (1/12)*d(s6)/s6, so even the THEORETICAL FLOOR where recon+R-solve were FREE (impossible) is only ~8% geomean (1767us) -- still 3.8x behind #1.
